content: Routine vaccines are those that are recommended for all individuals in the United States based on their age and vaccination history. Routine vaccines are particularly important for travelers because, while many vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles, mumps, or chickenpox are uncommon in the United States due to widespread vaccination, they remain prevalent in other parts of the world. If you are not vaccinated, international travel increases your risk of contracting and spreading these diseases. It is essential to ensure that you are up-to-date on all routine vaccinations. These vaccines protect you from infectious diseases, such as measles, which can spread rapidly among unvaccinated individuals. Although many of these diseases are rare in the United States, they are still common in other countries. Before traveling, consult the CDC’s destination pages for travel health information. These resources provide guidance on the vaccines or medications you may need and highlight the diseases or health risks specific to your destination. Schedule an appointment with your healthcare provider or a travel health specialist at least one month before your departure. They can assist you in obtaining destination-specific vaccines, medications, and information. Discussing your health concerns, travel itinerary, and planned activities with your provider allows them to offer tailored advice and recommendations. The specific routine vaccines you may need before traveling depend on factors such as your age, health status, and vaccination history. In some cases, you may require an accelerated vaccine schedule or a booster dose to ensure adequate protection before your trip.
